svg.text: TabM tanh N(0,1): one network holding K = 20 weight-sharing bCCNN submodels (R/tabm_bccnn.R, build_tabm; equations (T1)-(T8) of TabM_bCCNN_explained.md)
Every submodel is a (20, 15, 10) tanh network started exactly in the ccODP (chain-ladder) model; the submodels share the hidden weight matrices and differ only through cheap per-submodel vectors.
1 Input: one cell (i, j) of the triangle
3 Hidden layers of submodel k (the same picture holds for each of the 20 submodels)
three BatchEnsemble layers, widths 2 -> 20 -> 15 -> 10, activation tanh, dropout 0.1 after each (training only)
Layer d (T1): z_d^(k) = tanh( ((z_{d-1}^(k) o r_d^(k)) B_d) o s_d^(k) + c_d^(k) ), o = element-wise product
B_d is ONE matrix used by all 20 submodels (the sharing); r_d^(k), s_d^(k), c_d^(k) belong to submodel k only.
Per submodel this is a dense layer with weights diag(r) B diag(s) and bias c (T2): a full (20, 15, 10) tanh network.
Trainable: 490 shared (40 + 300 + 150) + 138 per submodel x 20 = 3,250 (+ 24 frozen embedding values).
Shape (n, K): one mean per cell
skip connection alpha_i + beta_j (bypasses the network entirely)
5 Initialisation (T6): every submodel starts as the ccODP model
Shared matrices B_1, B_2, B_3: Glorot uniform U(+-sqrt(6 / (q_{d-1} + q_d))) (Keras default), drawn once.
First adapter r_1^(k) in R^2: i.i.d. N(0, 1) per submodel k <- this configuration's ONLY source of
diversity at the start (TabM App. A.2 rule for embedding inputs; the '+-1' variant draws random signs).
r_2^(k) = r_3^(k) = 1, s_d^(k) = 1, c_d^(k) = 0: beyond the input scaling all 20 submodels begin identical.
Head: w^(k) = 0, w_0^(k) = c_hat (the ccODP intercept) => eta^(k) = c_hat at step 0 for every k.
Consequence: mu^(k)(i, j) = exp(alpha_i + beta_j + c_hat) = ccODP mean = chain-ladder cell, for all k,
before training: the ensemble reserve at step 0 IS the chain-ladder reserve; training moves it away.
Randomness: seed s in {0, ..., 4} fixes the Glorot draws, the r_1 draws and the dropout masks; 5 seeds averaged.
Embeddings: alpha, beta from the ccODP fit on the training triangle (stage 1) / full triangle (stage 2).
Loss (T4): the mean over the K submodels of the Poisson deviance loss,
each submodel scored on the SAME observed cells Y_ij:
L = (1/K) sum_k (1/n) sum_(i,j) [ mu^(k)(i,j) - Y_ij log mu^(k)(i,j) ]
Keras loss = 'poisson' on the (n, K) output with the target Y repeated in
K columns; equals the ODP deviance of Paper C up to a constant.
No coupling term: submodels interact only through the shared B_d.
Optimiser: RMSprop, learning rate 0.001, rho 0.9, eps 1e-7 (Listing 4);
full batch (all n cells in every step); dropout 0.1 while training.
Collective mean = arithmetic mean of the K
Reserve = sum of mu_bar over the lower
triangle (i + j > 11), per line of business.
claims are known to the last cell).
Individual submodel reserves show the spread
(1-4 % of the reserve at the elbow); the
collective deviance is <= the mean individual
